title: Taming the Loss Landscape of PINNs with Noisy Feynman–Kac Supervision: Operator Preconditioning and Non-Asymptotic Error Bounds
claim: The test problem has a periodic potential and source term that yield a structured, oscillatory reference solution.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, each heatmap with its own colorbar
description: Three square heatmaps in a row show the data for a 2-D Schrödinger-type PDE on the domain [-1,1]^2. The left panel, titled Potential, uses a grayscale colormap and shows a 4x4 lattice of bright and dark blobs, with values from about -9 to 9. The middle panel, Source term, uses a blue-white-red diverging colormap and shows a checkerboard-like pattern of alternating positive and negative lobes, with values from about -44 to 44. The right panel, Reference (FEM), uses a purple-to-orange diverging colormap and shows the solution, with strong dark-purple and brown lobes at the center and weaker blue and orange lobes near the edges. Each panel has x and y axes and a colorbar. The eye goes first to the saturated red and blue source term.
caption: Data for the Schrödinger-type equation [ref]. From left to right: potential $V(x)$, source $f(x)$, and FEM reference $\psi$.
abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often train slowly or fail to converge on challenging partial differential equations (PDEs), a behavior recently linked to severely ill-conditioned loss landscapes inherited from the underlying differential operator. We study PINNs augmented with a pointwise data-fidelity term, added at a few points in the domain to the standard residual and boundary losses. We show that this supervision term acts as an operator-level preconditioner: for suitable weights, our comparison bounds guarantee a substantially smaller condition number than under the standard PINN loss, independently of how the pointwise labels are obtained. For a broad class of PDEs admitting a Feynman-Kac (FK) representation, we generate such labels by Monte Carlo averages of the FK functional, resulting in what we call ``FK-PINNs", and using the excess risk decomposition approach, we derive non-asymptotic $L^2(Î©)$-error bounds for FK-PINNs with $\tanh$ activation trained by finitely many steps of gradient descent. Along the way, we establish pseudo-dimension bounds for first- and second-order derivatives of $\tanh$ neural networks, which are of independent interest and, to the best of our knowledge, new. Numerical experiments on Poisson, SchrÃ¶dinger, mean exit time, and committor problems corroborate the theory, and show that FK-PINNs can successfully solve PDEs for which standard PINNs exhibit severe failure modes.
